PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

MEMORANDUM

TO: Deal Team — Commercial Lease Engagement
FROM: Legal Counsel
DATE: [Current Date]
RE: Redline Analysis — Landlord's Counterparty Markup of Commercial Lease Agreement

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
I. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

We have reviewed the landlord's markup of the Commercial Lease Agreement (the "Markup") against our original draft and the firm's standard position, the applicable schedules and exhibits, and the deal team's controlling correspondence. This memorandum identifies each material deviation introduced by the counterparty's Markup, prioritizes each item, and recommends a response position.

The counterparty's revision accepts most firm-standard provisions but introduces three areas of material deviation: (1) the indemnification cap is reduced and the indemnity basket is converted from a deductible to a tipping basket; (2) the definition of Material Adverse Effect ("MAE") adds carve-outs for regulatory action; and (3) a new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations.

We have also reconciled these deviations against the governing schedules and exhibits, which control over general statements in the base lease materials. We expressly exclude from consideration any misfiled correspondence from unrelated engagements found in our matter folder.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
II. CONTROLLING INSTRUCTION — CLIENT PRIORITIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Per the controlling deal-team correspondence (the latest message in the thread), the client has authorized the following priorities:

• The client will concede the indemnification basket conversion (from deductible to tipping basket).
• Any reduction in the survival period for core representations is treated as a walk-away issue and must not be accepted.

Only the latest controlling message governs; earlier messages stating the opposite priority ordering are superseded.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
III. DEVIATION INVENTORY AND PRIORITIZED ANALYSIS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Counterparty Markup Change:
The indemnification cap is silently reduced from the firm-standard level, and the indemnity basket is converted from a deductible (first-dollar liability once the threshold is crossed) to a tipping basket (only the excess above the threshold is recoverable).

Reconciliation with Schedules:
Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that the counterparty's indemnification changes would silently shift. Under the original draft, those retained liabilities were carved out and subject to full indemnification above the deductible. Under the counterparts Markup, converting the basket to a tipping structure reduces the practical recovery available for those Schedule 5.2 liabilities because amounts below the basket threshold would never be recovered even once the threshold is crossed.

Priority: Medium

Analysis:
The basket conversion is a known economic concession that the client has decided to accept. The cap reduction, however, is a separate and significant deviation that must be distinguished from the basket conversion. While the client has authorized conceding the basket mechanics, the cap itself was not flagged as negotiable. Reducing the cap in the same provision as the basket conversion is a distinguishable change that should not be bundled with the concession the client authorized.

Recommended Response:
• ACCEPT the basket conversion from deductible to tipping basket, per the client's controlling instruction.
• REJECT the silent reduction in the indemnification cap. The cap reduction is a separate deviation from the basket mechanics and was not authorized. Reflag for negotiation at the original cap level. If the counterparty insists on the lower cap, quantify the exposure differential and escalate per the schedule 5.2 retained-liability analysis.
• Conform the indemnification scope for Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities so that the disclosed retained liabilities remain expressly carved out of any cap reduction, regardless of basket mechanics, to avoid silent shifting of those liabilities.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 2 — Material Adverse Effect (MAE) Definition — Regulatory Action Carve-Outs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Counterparty Markup Change:
The definition of Material Adverse Effect adds new carve-outs for regulatory action "of exactly the kind at issue in this matter."

Reconciliation with Schedules:
Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the counterparty's proposed MAE carve-outs. These are the very regulatory matters that the carve-out language is designed to exclude from the MAE definition. Under the original draft, the MAE definition did not exempt regulatory actions generally; the presence of the two pending inquiries on Schedule 3.7 means those specific matters are known and disclosed.

Priority: High

Analysis:
Adding a carve-out for regulatory action of the kind at issue in this matter is effectively a targeted exclusion designed to prevent the tenant from invoking an MAE based on the very regulatory exposures already disclosed on Schedule 3.7. This is material because:
• If accepted, it could eliminate the tenant's ability to withhold closing or terminate the lease if regulatory action materially impairs the premises or the tenant's use, even where such action has a materially adverse effect on the value or operations of the property.
• The two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 are precisely the regulatory actions the carve-out would sweep in. Accepting the carve-out would undermine the disclosure schedule regime by converting a disclosed risk into a blanket exemption.

The breadth of the carve-out ("regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter") is circular and would operate as a self-executing exclusion for the very regulatory risks the schedules already flag.

Recommended Response:
• REJECT the MAE carve-outs for regulatory action as drafted. The carve-out is overbroad and targeted directly at the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7.
• Offer a narrower alternative: exclude only regulatory actions that were already known and disclosed on Schedule 3.7 existing as of the execution date, provided the tenant's right to terminate based on MAE for undisclosed or future regulatory matters is preserved.
• If the counterparty insists on a regulatory carve-out, scope it to (i) actions resulting from a change in law or regulation of general applicability (not entity-specific), and (ii) actions that do not materially and disproportionately affect the Premises as compared to other similarly situated properties.
• Without this scoping, the carve-out undermines the purpose of the disclosure schedule regime.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 3 — Survival Period Reduction for Core Representations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Counterparty Markup Change:
A new limitation period shortens the survival period for the core representations beyond the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B.

Reconciliation with Schedules:
Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for representations and warranties, establishing the baseline period during which representations survive. The counterparty's proposed change contradicts Exhibit B.

Priority: HIGH — WALK-AWAY ITEM

Analysis:
Per the controlling deal-team correspondence, the client treats any survival-period reduction for the core representations as a walk-away issue. The counterparty's Markup proposes to shorten the survival period, which directly contradicts the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B and would materially impair the client's ability to bring claims for breach of core representations.

This is the most consequential deviation in the Markup. It is not merely an economic adjustment — it changes the fundamental risk allocation with respect to when claims can be brought. The representation survival periods are a cornerstone of the transaction risk framework, and any shortening materially reduces the client's protection.

Recommended Response:
• REJECT the survival-period reduction for the core representations. This is a walk-away issue per the client's controlling instruction.
• Reaffirm the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B as the controlling baseline.
• If the counterparty refuses to retract the survival-period reduction, coordinate with the client regarding next steps, up to and including termination/walk-away considerations.
• Do not offer any counterproposal that reduces survival below the Exhibit B matrix; any such offer would be outside the scope of authorized concessions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
IV. ADDITIONAL CONSIDERATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

The following considerations were also taken into account in this analysis:

1. Schedule 3.7 (Regulatory Inquiries): The two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7 are directly relevant to the MAE carve-out deviation analyzed above. Their existence underscores why the proposed regulatory carve-out is material — it targets precisely the disclosed regulatory exposure.

2. Schedule 5.2 (Retained Liabilities): The retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2 would be silently shifted by the indemnification changes if the cap reduction is combined with the basket conversion. The cap should be maintained at original levels for these disclosed retained liabilities.

3. Exhibit B (Survival Matrix): The survival matrix in Exhibit B establishes the baseline for representations survival. The counterparty's proposed limitation-period reduction contradicts the exhibit, and the client has designated this as a walk-away issue.

4. Misfiled correspondence: We note that certain administrative correspondence from unrelated engagements was found in the matter folder. Those documents were not relied upon in this analysis.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
V. SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------

| # | Deviation | Priority | Recommended Response |
|---|-----------|----------|---------------------|
| 1 | Indemnification cap reduction | Medium | REJECT the cap reduction; ACCEPT the basket conversion only |
| 2 | MAE regulatory-action carve-outs | High | REJECT as drafted; offer scoped alternative |
| 3 | Survival-period reduction | HIGH (walk-away) | REJECT outright; reaffirm Exhibit B survival matrix |

The counterparty's Markup presents three material deviations. Based on the controlling client instruction:
• The basket conversion (a component of Deviation 1) may be conceded.
• The survival-period reduction (Deviation 3) is a walk-away issue and must not be accepted under any circumstances.
• The MAE carve-outs (Deviation 2) are a high-priority item that requires a robust scoped counterproposal.

We recommend responding to the counterparty with a redline that (i) accepts the basket conversion, (ii) rejects the indemnification cap reduction at the reduced level and the MAE carve-outs as drafted, and (iii) firmly objects to the survival-period reduction as contrary to Exhibit B and unacceptable to the client.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------
PREPARED FOR INTERNAL DEAL TEAM USE ONLY
PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
